Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L08_GuidedPractice_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which plan best shows Unit 2 synthesis?

answer.text: A. A topic and three unrelated facts.

feedback.text: This lacks focus, organization, support, transitions, and format.

answer.text: B. A focus, logical points, support, reasoning, transitions, conclusion, and speech-ready notes.

feedback.text: Correct. This combines the major Unit 2 informative speech skills.

answer.text: C. A copied paragraph from a source.

feedback.text: This does not show paraphrase or speech-ready planning.

answer.text: D. A list of random speaking words.

feedback.text: Random words do not create an informative speech plan.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L08_GuidedPractice_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Source: Organized note cards help speakers remember the order of their ideas. Which paraphrase is accurate?

answer.text: A. Note cards make ideas unnecessary.

feedback.text: This changes the source meaning.

answer.text: B. Speakers should copy every word on note cards.

feedback.text: This adds an inaccurate idea.

answer.text: C. Note cards arranged clearly can help speakers keep their ideas in order.

feedback.text: Correct. This restates the source accurately in new wording.

answer.text: D. Organized notes do not affect speaking.

feedback.text: This contradicts the source meaning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L08_GuidedPractice_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.01

Which structure best explains steps for preparing a speech?

answer.text: A. Chronological order

feedback.text: Correct. Steps are easiest to understand in time order.

answer.text: B. Random order

feedback.text: Random order would confuse the process.

answer.text: C. Unrelated details

feedback.text: Unrelated details do not explain steps.

answer.text: D. Hidden structure

feedback.text: A hidden structure does not guide the audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L08_GuidedPractice_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which speech product is most presentation-ready?

answer.text: A. A full source paragraph to read.

feedback.text: This may cause reading instead of presenting.

answer.text: B. A title with no points.

feedback.text: This is incomplete because a presentation-ready plan needs organized points and support for the speaker to follow.

answer.text: C. A list of vague ideas.

feedback.text: Vague ideas do not guide delivery.

answer.text: D. Short notes with focus, points, support, transitions, and conclusion.

feedback.text: Correct. This format supports clear presentation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L08_GuidedPractice_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Which support best fits the point "Rehearsal improves timing"?

answer.text: A. Some rooms have clocks.

feedback.text: This is related to time but not rehearsal.

answer.text: B. A speaker can time each section during practice and shorten parts that run long.

feedback.text: Correct. This support directly explains the point.

answer.text: C. Timing is a word used in speeches.

feedback.text: This does not support the point.

answer.text: D. Some students enjoy speeches.

feedback.text: This is unrelated to timing.
